items.title: Fed's Goolsbee Warns Stubborn Inflation Could Force More Aggressive Rate Hikes — 'We're Not On Path Back To 2%'
items.excerpt: Goolsbee said inflationary pressures have persisted across several parts of the economy, including categories that cannot be easily explained by higher oil prices or tariffs. "If you look at how broad based the inflation is, it's not just that we're above the target and have been for some time. It's that in categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you're still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way," he said, while noting that there were some signs of trouble now for several months in a row. Goolsbee flagged services inflation and elevated healthcare costs, arguing that they are unlikely to ease simply because energy prices decline. "For me, keeping an eye on services inflation, which probably is not coming from tariffs or oil, is are some of the more troubling aspects of the inflation reports we've been getting for the last several months," he said. Goolsbee also cautioned against interpreting wage growth as an early warning sign of inflation, saying it tends to follow price increases rather than precede them. "Wage growth is not a leading indicator of inflation. It's actually a lagging indicator of inflation," he said. ... Goolsbee stopped short of committing to a specific rate decision, but made clear that the inflation trajectory would determine how aggressively the Fed needs to act. "If we continue to get stalled progress or even reverse progress, regress on inflation, then that's a totally different kettle of fish," he said. He also highlighted the AI data center buildout as a potential source of demand-driven inflation, pointing to rising construction costs, expensive computer chips and shortages of skilled workers.

items.title: Inflation will be key to future interest rate decisions: US Fed official
items.excerpt: Nov 15, 2026 San Diego [US], November 15: US Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip N Jefferson has said that inflation will be the key factor in determining future interest rate decisions, as price pressures remain elevated despite signs of stability in the American economy and labour market. Speaking at the University of California, San Diego Economic Roundtable on Friday, Jefferson said, "Accordingly, I see the trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal for determining the appropriate stance of monetary policy." He added, "Going forward, I believe that further policy adjustments should be determined by carefully examining trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks." Jefferson's remarks come as US inflation continues to remain well above the Federal Reserve's 2 per cent target. According to the data cited in his speech, the annual personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation rate stood at 3.6 per cent in September, while core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, was 3.1 per cent. Expressing concern over persistent price pressures, Jefferson said, "I remain concerned about the risk of higher energy prices leading to a persistent rise in inflation more broadly." He noted that higher energy costs were affecting sectors such as airfares and transportation, while strong demand for new technologies was also pushing up prices of certain goods, including memory chips. Jefferson said inflation data received so far for October remained consistent with price pressures staying well above the Fed's target. On the labour market, he said conditions had stabilised, with the unemployment rate standing at 4.1 per cent in October. "I expect the unemployment rate to stay around its current level in the near term-a level I view as consistent with maximum employment," he said. Jefferson also noted that the US economy had gained momentum this year, with gross domestic product (GDP) expanding at an annualised rate of 3.4 per cent in the third quarter. "The economy has gained momentum this year, expanding at a pace roughly in line with its potential," he said. Referring to the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) October meeting, Jefferson said he had joined the majority of policymakers in voting to keep interest rates unchanged. He said economic activity and labour market conditions had remained broadly solid since that meeting, while inflation readings continued to show persistent price pressures.

items.title: US consumer prices increase strongly for third straight month - Business Recorder
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON: US consumer prices increased more than expected in October, driven by higher costs for food and accommodation, leaving the Federal Reserve on course to raise interest rates next month. The Consumer Price Index report from the Labor Department on Tuesday also showed a strong buildup of underlying inflation pressures for the third straight month. The Labor Department’s Bureau of Labour Statistics did not publish year-over-year inflation readings because last year’s federal government shutdown prevented the collection of consumer price data in October 2025, leaving no comparison base. Annual consumer inflation jumped 3.7 percent in September. Inflation is running well above the US central bank’s 2 percent target. The US-Israeli war with Iran has boosted oil prices, combining with the import tariffs implemented by the Trump administration last year to lift the cost of living. High inflation contributed to the heavy losses suffered by President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections last week. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Tuesday that the US central bank should raise rates next month, adding that “a stronger policy move may be needed.” Waller also raised the prospect of a 50 basis point hike if core consumer prices, excluding food and energy, increased 0.3 percent or more from September, which they did. “Consumers’ inflation nightmare continues with no relief in sight,” said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. “Fed officials are going to need to bring a bigger hose if they have any hope of putting the inflation fire out.” The CPI increased 0.4 percent last month after advancing 0.6 percent in September. It was the third consecutive month of CPI gains of 0.4 percent or more. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the CPI climbing 0.3 percent over the month. Shelter, which includes rents, hotel and motel rooms, accounted for more than 30 percent of the increase in the CPI last month. Shelter costs rose 0.3 percent after climbing 0.4 percent in September. Food prices surged 0.5 percent after barely rising in the prior three months. Grocery store prices rebounded 0.4 percent, boosted by a 0.9 percent jump in the cost of beef. Egg prices rose 0.6 percent while fruits and vegetables were 0.6 percent more expensive. Prices for dairy and related products rose 0.6 percent. The cost of snacks surged 1.0 percent. Higher prices at the supermarket could be a reflection of more expensive diesel fuel. The cost of eating out also increased last month, with prices of food away from home surging 0.5 percent after rising 0.2 percent in September. The cost of full service meals increased 0.7 percent. Gasoline prices climbed 1.0 percent after soaring 9.1 percent. Though diesel prices have come down from record highs, they rose 2.7 percent last month after increasing 11.9 percent in September. STRONG CORE INFLATION Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the CPI increased 0.3 percent in October, advancing by the same margin for three months in a row. The so-called core CPI was forecast to have climbed 0.2 percent in October. Core CPI inflation increased 2.6 percent year-over-year in September. It was last month driven by a 0.3 percent rise in owners’ equivalent rent, a measure of the amount homeowners would pay to rent or would earn from renting their property. Prices for hotel and motel rooms rose 0.6 percent. Airline fares rose 0.4 percent. The cost of recreation increased 0.8 percent, while motor vehicle insurance advanced 0.7 percent. Household furnishings and supplies prices rebounded 0.7 percent, suggesting that some pass-through from tariffs remained.

items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 15 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: News· 15 Nov 2026· 7 min read Ramayana: Part 1 passed Jawan at the worldwide box office on its tenth day, and the rest of the week brought renewal news from Netflix, a first Eurovision Song Contest Asia winner, and four sets of Netflix departure dates. The figures below are as reported on 14 November 2026. ... ## Ramayana passes Jawan in ten days Ramayana: Part 1 reached Rs 1,228.00 crore worldwide by day 10, passing Jawan’s lifetime worldwide total of Rs 1,148.32 crore. The domestic picture tells the same story. Ramayana took Rs 819.50 crore gross in India against Jawan’s lifetime domestic gross of Rs 761.98 crore. Day 10 itself brought in Rs 72.90 crore net in India, from Rs 87.00 crore gross across 23,451 shows, and the ten day net total stood at Rs 685.60 crore. The Week reported the final day-10 figures from Sacnilk on 14 November 2026. The film’s first week grossed Rs 675.05 crore, and the second part is scheduled for Diwali 2028. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita and Yash plays Ravana. ## Trailers Nanhey Dil’s trailer is out ahead of its cinema release on 20 November 2026. Suniel Shetty plays a school principal who spots the talent of Raghu, a young boy whose father works as a dhobi, and gives him a place among children from wealthy families. Swarup Raj Medara wrote and directed the film, which was shot in 37 days and screened at the Toronto International Film Festival. Apple TV released the trailer for Fraggle Rock: A Holiday Gift, a new holiday special premiering globally on 4 December 2026. Nicole Scherzinger makes a special appearance and sings in the special, and Lilli Cooper returns as Doc and performs an original song. The story follows Wembley, who earns the title of Spirit Captain and has to return a treasured snow globe taken from Doc’s workshop. ## Renewals, casting and production Netflix renewed Earle Meets World for a second season of eight episodes. The renewal was announced on 12 November 2026, and no premiere date has been announced. Alix Earle returns with her family, and the first season drew 1.8 million views in its first three days. Netflix revealed the season 2 cast for Big Mistakes. Six stars return, one is promoted to series regular, and six new actors join. Filming wrapped in New Jersey, with additional filming in Palermo, Italy, and no premiere date has been announced. The series was created by Dan Levy and Rachel Sennott. VD13, the next film from Vijay Deverakonda and director Parasuram Petla, launched with a pooja ceremony in Hyderabad. Mrunal Thakur co-stars, Dil Raju produces, and shooting begins soon. The film is in pre-production and is the pair’s first film together since Geetha Govindam. Logan Lerman and Anna Van Patten joined the cast of Playmates, Searchlight’s coming of age drama directed by Lorraine Nicholson. Lerman plays Mr. Wick and Van Patten plays Jade, joining Lily-Rose Depp. The film follows 13 year old Elle, who considers the Playboy Mansion her second home. Bill Pullman plays Hugh Hefner. Still We Met added Emily Ratajkowski to its cast, alongside Mary Beth Barone and Joe Alwyn, with her role undisclosed. The film is Zackary Drucker’s directorial debut, from a script by Barone, and follows a night long hangout in New York that runs until sunrise. Aaron Pierre will star in Fairytale in New York, a Netflix and Lionsgate action thriller directed by Jalmari Helander. Set on Christmas Eve in New York City, it follows a cab driver whose estranged son’s gift is stolen, sending him on a night of vengeance. No release date has been announced. Jay and Silent Bob: Store Wars starts filming in about two weeks in Canada, Jason Mewes confirmed in a Collider interview. The sequel was announced in 2024 and has no release date. Mewes and Kevin Smith return, with the story picking up after Clerks III as the pair run a legal marijuana dispensary and face a rival shop across the street. Law & Order: SVU goes on a brief Thanksgiving hiatus after its 600th episode, which aired on 12 November 2026 and brought Christopher Meloni back as Elliot Stabler. The next episode, “Untouchable”, airs on 3 December 2026 as the fall finale, with Rick Gonzalez returning as Detective Bobby Reyes. Stephanie March also returns as Assistant DA Alexandra Cabot after eight years, though her episode has not been announced. ## Awards Cinema Eye Honors announced the nominations for its 20th annual honours on 12 November 2026. You Can See Everything and American Doctor lead with seven nominations each. The winners will be announced on 11 January 2027 in New York. Five shorts are in the running for European Short Film, named by the European Film Academy at the Seville European Film Festival on 13 November 2026: God is Shy, L’Mina, Morning Circle, The End and Unleaded 95. The winners will be announced at the ceremony in Athens on 16 January 2027. The main European Film Awards nominations followed on 14 November 2026 at the Thessaloniki Film Festival. Fatherland leads with 11 nominations, followed by La Bola Negra with 10. The winners will be announced in Athens on 16 January 2027. CARMELLE of the Philippines won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok on 14 November 2026, with 211 points for “Sobra-Sobra”, 93 from the juries and 118 from the public vote. Thailand finished second with 170 points and Vietnam third with 164. Artists from 11 countries took part. ## Streaming departures Alien (1979) and Aliens (1986) leave Netflix in the US on 1 December 2026, as of 15 November 2026. The Karate Kid films leave Netflix in the US on 1 December 2026, as of 15 November 2026: the 1984 original, Karate Kid Part II, Karate Kid Part III and the 2010 remake, The Karate Kid, depart together. The Resident, Fox’s six season medical drama, leaves Netflix on 20 November 2026, as of 15 November 2026. Its final day to watch is 20 November, and it is also available on Hulu for now. True Romance, the 1993 crime film written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by Tony Scott, leaves Netflix on 19 November 2026, as of 15 November 2026. No new streaming home has been announced.

items.excerpt: Phil Collins cries, Billy Idol shouts and rappers romp at Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony has been a lively celebration. Phil Collins gave a tearful acceptance speech, while Cynthia Erivo delivered an electrifying tribute. Oprah Winfrey inducted the late Luther Vandross, and Wu-Tang Clan brought a rowdy celebration to the stage. Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte, Sade, Joy Division/New Order, and Iron Maiden were also inducted. U2 surprised the audience by opening the night, and Run DMC and Aerosmith closed with a loud jam. Despite some absences, the event was vibrant and memorable, with performances and tributes that kept the crowd engaged.
